header.name: STAGE WP6 — 10-Year Incident Multimorbidity Prediction Pipeline
header.developer: BCN-AIM Research Lab, Universitat de Barcelona (UB)
header.global_availability: Not publicly deployed. Research-use within STAGE consortium; downstream integration via SRDC (CDS) and ABACUS (health monitoring app).
header.regulatory_status: Not applicable at current stage. Designed with EU AI Act (Articles 9, 13) and FUTURE-AI guideline alignment for potential future high-risk AI classification.

summary: The STAGE WP6 pipeline predicts 10-year incident risk for 27 chronic conditions using UK Biobank data (N≈502,462; Application 295277). The architecture consists of 26 independent LightGBM classifiers plus 1 XGBoost for Substance Use Disorder (with Depression out-of-fold probability augmentation), each trained on disease-specific top-50 features. The pipeline incorporates a trustworthy AI stack: fairness auditing, Platt scaling calibration, SHAP explainability, and co-creation with clinicians, researchers, and citizens.

intended_use.primary: Clinical decision support — inform clinicians of 10-year incident risk for chronic conditions to support proactive, preventive care planning.
intended_use.target_population: Adults aged 40–69 at UK Biobank baseline (2006–2010 recruitment), with external validation planned on NFBC1966 (Finnish birth cohort, born 1966).
intended_settings: Primary care (via SRDC CDS Hooks integration)
Personalized coaching (via LIVA Health, KORA study)
intended_use.human_oversight_description: All predictions are clinician-mediated. The pipeline is designed as a decision-support tool, not an autonomous diagnostic system. Predictions should be interpreted alongside clinical judgment and patient context.

cautioned_out_of_scope_uses: Not for acute clinical decisions or emergency triage.
Not validated outside UKB-equivalent populations (predominantly White British, UK-resident, age 40–69 at baseline).
Not intended for individual diagnostic confirmation — risk scores are population-level estimates.
Not validated for populations under 40 or over 70 at time of prediction.
Not intended for use without clinician interpretation.

imdrf_risk_classification.description: IMDRF SaMD risk classification varies per disease. All predictions are 'inform' purpose. Condition significance varies.
imdrf_risk_classification.note: Full per-disease IMDRF classification to be finalized with WP2 embedded ethics team (TUM).

training_data.geographic_scope: 22 assessment centres across England, Scotland, and Wales
training_data.outcome_ascertainment: Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) ICD-10 codes; three-tier prevalent exclusion (ICD, medication, survey-based)
training_data.split_strategy: Geographic hold-out (training: non-London centres; test: London centres)
training_data.healthy_volunteer_bias: UK Biobank participants are healthier, wealthier, and more educated than the UK general population. This is a known, documented selection bias that affects generalizability.
training_data.ethnic_composition: Approximately 94% White British. Non-White subgroups have smaller sample sizes, which may reduce model reliability for these populations.

known_limitations: Label ascertainment relies on hospital ICD-10 codes; conditions managed entirely in primary care may be underascertained.
Temporal context: baseline features collected 2006–2010; clinical practice and population health profiles have evolved.
Healthy volunteer bias: UKB participants are not representative of the UK general population.
Ethnic composition: ~94% White British — model performance for non-White subgroups requires careful interpretation.
GP-linkage-based incident outcomes deferred to after UKB-RAP restoration (September 2026).
Five diseases excluded from deployment: Dementia, Parkinson's Disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Sleep Disorders, Severe Mental Illness.

internal.method: Geographic hold-out (London vs non-London assessment centres)

external_nfbc1966.blocker: Findata permit transition; workaround via Iiro (UOULU) running validation inside Kapseli secure environment

external_ukb_rap.blocker: UKB-RAP (DNAnexus) platform suspended since April 2026; restoration expected September 2026
external_ukb_rap.planned: GP-linkage outcome validation, additional sensitivity analyses

fairness_audit.approach: Per-disease × per-subgroup evaluation on geographic hold-out test set

bias_mitigation.tautological_feature_exclusion: Disease-specific biomarker features that could create circular predictions are excluded before feature selection (e.g., HbA1c excluded from Diabetes model).
bias_mitigation.prevalent_case_exclusion: Three-tier exclusion (ICD, medication, survey-based) removes participants with prevalent conditions from training to prevent information leakage.
bias_mitigation.co_creation_provenance: Pipeline design informed by multi-stakeholder co-creation (STAGE WP2/WP3): clinicians, researchers, ethicists, and citizens. Requirements include SHAP explainability, life-stage-specific models, clinician-mediated predictions, and fairness auditing.

explainability.scope: Per-prediction waterfall plots showing top feature attributions with directional contributions
explainability.global_importance: LightGBM gain-based feature importance used for top-k selection (k=50 per disease)
explainability.modifiable_risk_factors: Identified per disease; flagged for counterfactual scenario generation ('what if you stop smoking?')

environmental_impact.note: Emissions tracked during training runs on Sauron server. Full carbon footprint to be reported in D6.2.

data_governance.data_sharing_constraints: Per-sample SHAP matrices cannot be shared with SRDC under Application 295277. Synthetic distribution approach (binned conditional summaries with PCHIP inverse-CDF) used instead.
data_governance.nfbc_dta: Signed DTA (University of Oulu → UB/BCN-AIM) in place for NFBC1966 validation.
data_governance.withdrawn_participants: Handled natively on DNAnexus; gracefully optional in shared code.

key_requirements_from_stakeholders: EHR integration via standards-based CDS Hooks
co_creation.documentation: STAGE co-creation paper (WP2/WP3 methodology); Álvaro co-author
